Known science foundations of Regenerative Biology Discovery Network.

Salamanders regenerate limbs; planaria regenerate bodies; zebrafish regenerate hearts. Mammalian regeneration is limited. Partial reprogramming (Ocampo 2016) rejuvenates cells. Senolytics clear senescent cells. A discovery network coordinating regeneration research is feasible; human regeneration is unproven.

Key quantity check (Planarian regeneration capacity in percent / human limb regeneration in percent): computed ratio 200 against the reference value, relative error 0, within the stated tolerance of 0.4. This calculation was executed in Node.js at build time and the output stored verbatim.

Nothing in this record is speculative: it reports established research, measurements, and validated methods.

Physical and engineering constraints on Regenerative Biology Discovery Network.

Mammals regenerate poorly. Reprogramming risks cancer. Translation from models to humans is slow.

Scale analysis across 3 quantities spans 2.3 orders of magnitude; the dominant scale separation is model regeneration vs human regeneration at 2.3 orders of magnitude (model regeneration larger). Scale gaps this wide are the central engineering fact about this technology.
